data: Corpus inscriptionum Latinarum. X: Inscriptiones Bruttiorum, Lucaniae, Campaniae, Siciliae, Sardiniae Latinae. Pars I: Inscriptiones Bruttiorum, Lucaniae, Campaniae

T. Mommsen, ed., Corpus inscriptionum Latinarum. X: Inscriptiones Bruttiorum, Lucaniae, Campaniae, Siciliae, Sardiniae Latinae. Pars I: Inscriptiones Bruttiorum, Lucaniae, Campaniae, 1st edn, vol. 10, 17 vols, Corpus Inscriptionum Latinarum, 10.1 (Berlin; New York: G. Reimer; de Gruyter, 1883), https://cil.bbaw.de/en/homenavigation/the-cil/volumes
The remains of one line of Greek letters, preceded by a plain cross (which may be a later addition), are preserved on the moulding at the base of the relief.

Slightly irregularly disposed letters, with a hedera between the first two words. In the text preserved by Gualtherus lunate epsilon, sigma and cursive omega are recorded, and interpuncts before the numerals.
Later 2nd century CE or first half of 3rd century CE

Four complete lines of Latin text approximately centred
Text is shallowly incised, irregular and rough. Letters are not straight, nor in line with each other. Very basic serifs, on occasional letters. Long tail on "L" in line 4.
Ferrua dates to the fourth century on the basis of the lettering.
